category: Simscape, code generation, hardware support, editor tools & file types (extended)
description: Simscape language build tools, key Foundation library and Simscape Multibody blocks and Simscape logging; Simulink Coder/Embedded Coder targets, storage classes and code mappings, Legacy Code Tool, TLC, HDL Coder and PLC Coder entry points; hardware support packages and blocksets; the Simulink editor tools not covered elsewhere; and the file types used across the Simulink product family.

tools.name: ssc_build
tools.description: Builds a custom Simscape block library from a package folder (+pkg) of Simscape language source files (.ssc). Each component file becomes a block in the generated library model pkg_lib.slx.
tools.usage:
ssc_build(package)
ssc_build   % in the parent folder of the package
tools.example:
% +MyComponents/myResistor.ssc contains:
% component myResistor < foundation.electrical.branch
%   parameters, R = {1, 'Ohm'}; end
%   equations, v == i*R; end
% end
ssc_build('MyComponents');
open_system('MyComponents_lib');
tools.notes: Use ssc_protect to ship obfuscated .sscp files. A single .ssc file can also be used without building a library through the Simscape Component block.

tools.name: Electrical Reference
tools.description: Simscape Foundation block representing electrical ground (zero voltage). Every electrical network needs at least one Electrical Reference, together with a Solver Configuration block.
tools.usage: Simscape > Foundation Library > Electrical > Electrical Elements > Electrical Reference  |  add_block('fl_lib/Electrical/Electrical Elements/Electrical Reference', [mdl '/GND'])
tools.example:
add_block('fl_lib/Electrical/Electrical Elements/Electrical Reference', [mdl '/GND']);
add_line(mdl, 'C1/RConn1', 'GND/LConn1', 'autorouting', 'on');
tools.notes: Physical ports are addressed as LConn/RConn in add_line. Missing references cause 'no reference node' compile errors.

tools.name: Capacitor
tools.description: Linear capacitor i = C dv/dt from the Simscape Foundation electrical library, with optional series resistance (ESR) and parallel leakage conductance. The capacitor voltage is a state whose initial value can be set with priority.
tools.usage: Simscape > Foundation Library > Electrical > Electrical Elements > Capacitor  |  add_block('fl_lib/Electrical/Electrical Elements/Capacitor', [mdl '/C1'])
tools.example:
add_block('fl_lib/Electrical/Electrical Elements/Capacitor', [mdl '/C1']);
set_param([mdl '/C1'], 'C', '47e-6');
tools.notes: Units are separate parameters (e.g. C_unit) editable in the dialog. Initial voltage is set under Initial Targets.

tools.name: Controlled Voltage Source
tools.description: Ideal voltage source whose voltage equals a physical signal input, bridging Simulink control logic (through a Simulink-PS Converter) and an electrical network. Use it for PWM averages, test waveforms or driving circuits from computed signals.
tools.usage: Simscape > Foundation Library > Electrical > Electrical Sources > Controlled Voltage Source
tools.notes: Ideal sources in parallel with capacitors or in loops with other ideal voltage sources create dependent-state errors.

tools.name: Mechanical Rotational Reference
tools.description: Simscape Foundation block representing a fixed (zero angular velocity) reference point, such as a housing or ground, for rotational mechanical networks.
tools.usage: Simscape > Foundation Library > Mechanical > Rotational Elements > Mechanical Rotational Reference
tools.example: add_block('fl_lib/Mechanical/Rotational Elements/Mechanical Rotational Reference', [mdl '/Housing']);
tools.notes: Use Mechanical Translational Reference for translational networks.

tools.name: Inertia
tools.description: Ideal rotational inertia T = J dw/dt from the Simscape Foundation mechanical library. It can have one port (side connection) or two graphical ports (series connection) with identical behaviour.
tools.usage: Simscape > Foundation Library > Mechanical > Rotational Elements > Inertia
tools.example: add_block('fl_lib/Mechanical/Rotational Elements/Inertia', [mdl '/Rotor']);
tools.notes: Positive direction is from the port to the reference; the inertia's angular velocity is a state.

tools.name: Ideal Torque Source
tools.description: Generates a torque proportional to its physical signal input between its two rotational ports, regardless of their velocities. Used to apply control or load torques to mechanical networks.
tools.usage: Simscape > Foundation Library > Mechanical > Mechanical Sources > Ideal Torque Source
tools.example: add_block('fl_lib/Mechanical/Mechanical Sources/Ideal Torque Source', [mdl '/Tload']);
tools.notes: Connect port C to a Mechanical Rotational Reference to apply torque relative to ground.

tools.name: powergui
tools.description: Environment block required by Simscape Electrical Specialized Power Systems models; it selects continuous, discrete or phasor simulation, sets the discrete sample time and opens analysis tools (steady state, load flow, FFT, impedance).
tools.usage: Simscape > Electrical > Specialized Power Systems > powergui (one per model, at the top level)
tools.example:
% place powergui once at the top level of an SPS model and choose Discrete with Ts = 50e-6
open_system('power_3phseriescomp');
tools.notes: The Specialized Power Systems library was removed in R2026a; migrate models to Simscape Electrical blocks with spsConversionAssistant or spsConversionFindBlocks.

tools.name: World Frame
tools.description: Simscape Multibody block providing the inertial world reference frame, the ultimate ground of every multibody model. Bodies attached rigidly to it are fixed in space.
tools.usage: Simscape > Multibody > Frames and Transforms > World Frame  |  add_block('sm_lib/Frames and Transforms/World Frame', [mdl '/World'])
tools.notes: A new multibody model (smnew) contains World Frame, Mechanism Configuration and Solver Configuration preconnected.

tools.name: Rigid Transform
tools.description: Maintains a fixed rotation and translation between a base frame (B) and a follower frame (F). It is the basic way to position bodies, joints and sensors relative to each other in Simscape Multibody.
tools.usage: Simscape > Multibody > Frames and Transforms > Rigid Transform

parameters.name: Rotation method
parameters.description: None, Aligned Axes, Standard Axis, Arbitrary Axis, Rotation Sequence, Rotation Matrix or Quaternion.

parameters.name: Translation method
parameters.description: None, Cartesian, Standard Axis or Cylindrical.

tools.example:
add_block('sm_lib/Frames and Transforms/Rigid Transform', [mdl '/ArmOffset']);
% dialog: Translation = Cartesian, Offset = [0.5 0 0] m
tools.notes: Chain Rigid Transforms to build complex geometry; use simscape.multibody.RigidTransform for programmatic multibody construction.

tools.name: Brick Solid
tools.description: Simscape Multibody solid with box geometry centred on its reference frame. It adds mass and inertia (computed from geometry and density or mass, or custom) and 3-D visualization to a body.
tools.usage: Simscape > Multibody > Body Elements > Brick Solid

parameters.name: Inertia Type / Based on / Density
parameters.description: Calculate from Geometry (by density 1000 kg/m^3 or mass), Custom, or Point Mass.

tools.example:
add_block('sm_lib/Body Elements/Brick Solid', [mdl '/Link1']);
% dialog: Dimensions = [0.5 0.05 0.05] m, Density = 2700 kg/m^3
tools.notes: Other solids: Cylindrical, Spherical, Ellipsoidal, Extruded, Revolved and File Solid (CAD geometry).

tools.name: Prismatic Joint
tools.description: Joint with one translational degree of freedom along the common z-axis of its base (B) and follower (F) frames. Supports internal spring/damper, position limits, force or motion actuation and sensing outputs.
tools.usage: Simscape > Multibody > Joints > Prismatic Joint

parameters.name: Internal Mechanics
parameters.description: Equilibrium position, spring stiffness and damping.

parameters.name: Limits
parameters.description: Upper/lower bounds with stiffness, damping and transition region.

parameters.name: Actuation
parameters.description: Force: None/Provided by Input/Automatically Computed; Motion: Provided by Input/Automatically Computed.

parameters.name: Sensing
parameters.description: Position, velocity, acceleration and force outputs.

tools.example:
add_block('sm_lib/Joints/Prismatic Joint', [mdl '/Slider']);
% enable Actuation > Force = Provided by Input to expose the f port
tools.notes: Joint mode (Normal, Locked, Disengaged) can be switched by an input port. Revolute Joint is the rotational counterpart.

tools.name: Mechanism Configuration
tools.description: Sets mechanism-wide properties of a Simscape Multibody network: uniform gravity (constant, time-varying or none), linearization perturbation and Newton iterations for joint mode transitions.
tools.usage: Simscape > Multibody > Utilities > Mechanism Configuration

parameters.name: nonlinearIterations
parameters.description: Newton iterations for joint transitions, default 2.

tools.example:
add_block('sm_lib/Utilities/Mechanism Configuration', [mdl '/Mech']);
set_param([mdl '/Mech'], 'gravity', '[0 -9.81 0]');
tools.notes: At most one per multibody network; without it gravity defaults to zero.

tools.name: Transform Sensor
tools.description: Measures the relative rotation, translation, velocities and accelerations between a base (B) and follower (F) frame in Simscape Multibody, outputting the selected quantities as physical signals.
tools.usage: Simscape > Multibody > Frames and Transforms > Transform Sensor

parameters.name: Rotation
parameters.description: Angle, axis, quaternion, rotation matrix or rotation sequence outputs.

parameters.name: Measurement frame
parameters.description: Observation and expressed-in frames: World, Base or Follower.

tools.example:
add_block('sm_lib/Frames and Transforms/Transform Sensor', [mdl '/TipPos']);
% select Translation > X, Y, Z; connect outputs through PS-Simulink Converter blocks
tools.notes: Joint blocks have their own sensing ports for joint-coordinate quantities.

tools.name: smimport
tools.description: Imports a CAD assembly (exported via Simscape Multibody Link as XML), a URDF robot description or a Robotics System Toolbox rigidBodyTree into a new Simscape Multibody model with solids, rigid transforms and joints.
tools.usage:
[mdl, dataFile] = smimport(fileName)
smimport(fileName, Name, Value)
smimport(rigidBodyTree)

parameters.name: fileName
parameters.description: Multibody description XML or URDF file.

parameters.name: DataFileName
parameters.description: MATLAB file for imported parameters (XML import).

tools.example: smimport('robotArm.urdf', 'ModelName', 'robotArm_sm');
tools.notes: CAD import requires the Simscape Multibody Link plug-in for SolidWorks, Creo or Inventor to export the XML and geometry files.

tools.name: sscexplore
tools.description: Opens the Simscape Results Explorer for a simulation log (simlog) so you can browse the node tree of logged variables and plot them. Logging is enabled with the SimscapeLogType model parameter.
tools.usage:
sscexplore(node)
sscexplore(node, nodepath)

parameters.name: nodepath
parameters.description: Path of a sub-node to open at.

tools.notes: SimscapeLogType values: 'none', 'all', 'local' (only blocks with logging enabled). For long simulations, logged data can be streamed to disk instead of memory (Simscape pane options).

tools.name: simscape.logging.Node
tools.description: Hierarchical object holding Simscape logged data; child nodes mirror the block hierarchy and leaf nodes contain simscape.logging.Series with time, values and units. Use it to extract variables from simlog programmatically.
tools.usage:
node = simlog.<block>.<variable>
s = node.series; t = s.time; v = s.values('unit')

parameters.name: series
parameters.description: simscape.logging.Series with time and values(unit) methods.

parameters.name: plot / print / find
parameters.description: Plot, print or search the node tree.

tools.notes: simscape.logging.import and simscape.logging.export read and write logs to MLDATX files.

tools.name: rtwbuild
tools.description: Legacy command that generates and builds code for a model according to its system target file. Since R2021a it is an alias of slbuild and is not recommended for new scripts.
tools.usage:
rtwbuild(model)
rtwbuild(subsystem)
tools.example: rtwbuild('myModel');   % prefer slbuild('myModel')
tools.notes: rtwrebuild rebuilds from existing generated code without regenerating.

tools.name: grt.tlc
tools.description: Generic Real-Time system target file of Simulink Coder. It generates portable C/C++ with a standard rt_main and builds a host executable, suited to rapid prototyping, batch simulation and external mode on the host.
tools.usage: set_param(mdl, 'SystemTargetFile', 'grt.tlc'); slbuild(mdl)

parameters.name: MatFileLogging
parameters.description: Log outputs to a MAT-file from the executable.

tools.notes: Use ert.tlc (Embedded Coder) for production code with interface control and optimizations.

tools.name: ert.tlc
tools.description: Embedded Real-Time system target file of Embedded Coder for production embedded C/C++: configurable function interfaces, code mappings and storage classes, code optimizations, traceability reports, and SIL/PIL verification. Variants include ert_shrlib.tlc for shared libraries.
tools.usage: set_param(mdl, 'SystemTargetFile', 'ert.tlc'); slbuild(mdl)

parameters.name: SupportContinuousTime / SupportNonFinite
parameters.description: Enable features excluded by default for embedded targets.

tools.notes: Requires Embedded Coder. The Code Generation Advisor can tune settings for efficiency, traceability or safety.

tools.name: ExportedGlobal
tools.description: Built-in storage class that makes a signal, state or parameter a global variable defined in the generated model.c and declared in model.h, so external code can read or write it. Related built-ins: ImportedExtern (declared extern, defined by external code), ImportedExternPointer, and Embedded Coder classes such as Const, Volatile, Define, GetSet, Struct and ExportToFile.
tools.usage:
Code Mappings editor > Data > Storage Class = ExportedGlobal
setSignal(cm, portHandle, 'StorageClass', 'ExportedGlobal')
paramObj.CoderInfo.StorageClass = 'ExportedGlobal'
tools.notes: Data with an explicit storage class is not optimized away, which can cost memory and speed; apply it only to interface data.

tools.name: coder.mapping.api.get
tools.description: Returns the code mappings object (coder.mapping.api.CodeMapping) of a model, whose methods configure storage classes of inports, outports, signals, states, parameters and data stores, and function names and templates for model entry-point functions. It is the scriptable form of the Code Mappings editor.
tools.usage: cm = coder.mapping.api.get(model)

parameters.name: setDataDefault / getDataDefault
parameters.description: Default storage class per data category.

parameters.name: setFunction / setFunctionDefault
parameters.description: Entry-point function names, customization templates and memory sections.

tools.notes: Requires Embedded Coder for most settings. Code mappings replace the older approach of setting storage classes on Simulink.Signal/Parameter objects.

tools.name: legacy_code
tools.description: Legacy Code Tool: generates, compiles and wraps a C MEX S-function (and optional TLC file for inlined code generation) that calls an existing C/C++ function, from a MATLAB structure describing the function signature. The fastest route to reuse legacy algorithms in simulation and generated code.
tools.usage:
def = legacy_code('initialize')
legacy_code('sfcn_cmex_generate', def)
legacy_code('compile', def)
legacy_code('slblock_generate', def, modelName)
legacy_code('sfcn_tlc_generate', def)

parameters.name: OutputFcnSpec
parameters.description: Prototype of the function called at each step, e.g. 'double y1 = doubleIt(double u1)'.

tools.notes: For simple calls the C Caller block needs no generated S-function at all.

tools.name: Target Language Compiler
tools.description: The template language and engine (TLC) that Simulink Coder uses to turn the compiled model description (model.rtw) into source code. System target files (grt.tlc, ert.tlc) and block target files for inlined S-functions are written in TLC with directives such as %function, %assign and %<expr>.
tools.usage:
%% sfun_gain.tlc
%implements sfun_gain "C"
%function Outputs(block, system) Output
  %<LibBlockOutputSignal(0, "", "", 0)> = %<LibBlockInputSignal(0, "", "", 0)> * 2;
%endfunction

parameters.name: %implements
parameters.description: Associates the TLC file with an S-function or block type and language.

tools.notes: Direct TLC authoring is rarely needed today; Legacy Code Tool, C Caller and code mappings cover most integration cases.

tools.name: plcgeneratecode
tools.description: Simulink PLC Coder command that generates IEC 61131-3 Structured Text (and optionally ladder diagrams) for an atomic subsystem, targeting IDEs such as CODESYS, TwinCAT, RSLogix/Studio 5000, TIA Portal and others.
tools.usage: generatedFiles = plcgeneratecode(subsystem)

parameters.name: subsystem
parameters.description: Path of an atomic subsystem configured for PLC code generation.

parameters.name: PLC_TargetIDE (configuration)
parameters.description: Target IDE selected in Configuration Parameters > PLC Code Generation.

tools.example:
plcopenconfigset('plcdemo_simple_subsystem/SimpleSubsystem');
files = plcgeneratecode('plcdemo_simple_subsystem/SimpleSubsystem');
tools.notes: Blocks and data types are limited to what PLC targets support; run plccheckforladder/Model Advisor PLC checks first.

tools.name: hdlsetup
tools.description: Sets a model's configuration parameters (fixed-step discrete solver, single-tasking, diagnostics and more) to values required or recommended for HDL code generation with HDL Coder. Run it once before makehdl.
tools.usage: hdlsetup(modelName)
tools.notes: hdlsetup changes several settings with set_param; commit the model first so the changes are easy to review.

tools.name: Simulink Support Package for Arduino Hardware
tools.description: Add-on that provides Simulink blocks for Arduino boards (digital and analog I/O, PWM, serial, I2C, SPI, CAN on supported boards, WiFi, sensors) and a build flow that generates code and deploys it to the board, plus Monitor & Tune (external mode) for live tuning.
tools.usage: Install via Add-On Explorer; Configuration Parameters > Hardware Implementation > Hardware board = 'Arduino Uno' (or other); Hardware tab > Build, Deploy & Start or Monitor & Tune

parameters.name: Digital Input / Digital Output / Analog Input / PWM
parameters.description: Core I/O blocks configured by pin number.

tools.notes: Blocks run on the board only; in normal simulation most I/O blocks output zeros. Code generation for Arduino does not require Embedded Coder.

tools.name: Simulink Support Package for Raspberry Pi Hardware
tools.description: Add-on providing blocks for Raspberry Pi GPIO, camera, audio, I2C, SPI, serial, UDP/TCP and sense HAT peripherals, and a flow that generates Linux code, builds it on the Pi and runs it standalone or in external mode.
tools.usage: Install via Add-On Explorer; Hardware board = 'Raspberry Pi'; Hardware tab > Build, Deploy & Start or Monitor & Tune

parameters.name: V4L2 Video Capture / UDP Send / UDP Receive

tools.notes: Board credentials are configured in the model's Hardware Implementation pane or with raspberrypi() in MATLAB.

tools.name: STM32 Microcontroller Blockset
tools.description: MathWorks product (successor of the Embedded Coder Support Package for STMicroelectronics STM32 Processors) that adds STM32 peripheral driver blocks, STM32CubeMX integration, CMSIS optimizations and one-click code generation and deployment to STM32 MCUs with Embedded Coder.
tools.usage: Install via Add-On Explorer; Hardware board = STM32 board; configure peripherals with STM32CubeMX project

parameters.name: Peripheral blocks
parameters.description: ADC, PWM/timers, GPIO, UART, SPI, I2C, CAN blocks bound to the CubeMX configuration.

tools.example:
% Hardware Implementation > Hardware board = 'STM32F4-Discovery' (for example)
% Hardware tab > Build, Deploy & Start
tools.notes: Requires Embedded Coder; supports PIL and external mode over serial.

tools.name: C2000 Microcontroller Blockset
tools.description: Simulink blockset for Texas Instruments C2000 real-time MCUs used in digital power conversion and motor control: ePWM, ADC, eCAP, eQEP, SCI, SPI, CAN and IPC blocks, IQmath fixed-point support, interrupt-driven scheduling, PIL and external mode.
tools.usage: Install via Add-On Explorer; Hardware board = 'TI Delfino F28379D LaunchPad' (for example); build with Embedded Coder

parameters.name: ePWM / ADC
parameters.description: Timer-based PWM generation and synchronized ADC sampling.

tools.example:
% configure ePWM to trigger ADC SOC, run the control loop in a Hardware Interrupt-driven subsystem, then
% Hardware tab > Build, Deploy & Start
tools.notes: Commonly combined with Motor Control Blockset reference applications for field-oriented control.

tools.name: Model Data Editor
tools.description: Spreadsheet-style editor of a model's data items (inports/outports, signals, data stores, states and parameters) where you can sort, group, filter and edit names, data types, dimensions, units, min/max and storage settings without hunting through the diagram.
tools.usage: Modeling tab > Model Data Editor (Ctrl+Shift+E)

parameters.name: Tabs
parameters.description: Inports/Outports, Signals, Data Stores, States, Parameters.

tools.example: % open vdp, press Ctrl+Shift+E, select the Signals tab and set DataType = single for selected rows
tools.notes: Selections in the table highlight the corresponding lines and blocks in the diagram.

tools.name: Property Inspector
tools.description: Docked panel that shows and edits the parameters and properties of the current selection (block, line, port, annotation or the model itself), updating as you click through the diagram. Faster than opening block dialogs one by one.
tools.usage: Modeling tab > Property Inspector (Ctrl+Shift+I)

parameters.name: Parameters / Properties / Info tabs
parameters.description: Block parameters, properties such as callbacks and priorities, and descriptions.

tools.example: % select a Gain block with the Property Inspector open and change Gain directly in the panel
tools.notes: With nothing selected it shows model properties such as callbacks and description.

tools.name: Schedule Editor
tools.description: Tool that shows the partitions of a model (rates, export functions, explicit partitions of atomic subsystems and referenced models) as a data-dependency graph and an ordered table, and lets you change their execution order for simulation and code generation.
tools.usage: Modeling tab > Schedule Editor

parameters.name: Order table
parameters.description: Execution order of partitions; drag to reorder.

tools.example:
% mark an atomic subsystem as a partition: Block Parameters > Execution > Partition type = Explicit
% then Modeling > Schedule Editor and reorder the partitions
tools.notes: The schedule can also be read and set programmatically through the model's Schedule parameter.

tools.name: Diagnostic Viewer
tools.description: Window listing errors, warnings and information messages from model updates, simulations and builds, grouped by stage, with links to the offending blocks and suggested fixes.
tools.usage: Debug tab > Diagnostics, or click the warning/error link in the status bar

parameters.name: Stages
parameters.description: Messages grouped by operation (Update Diagram, Simulation, Build).

tools.notes: Diagnostic severity is configured in the Diagnostics pane of Configuration Parameters.

tools.name: .slx
tools.description: Default Simulink model and library file format since R2012a: a compressed Open Packaging Conventions (zip) container with the block diagram in XML plus embedded data such as images and model workspace contents.
tools.usage:
save_system(mdl)                      % default format
save_system(mdl, 'copy.slx')
tools.example: new_system('demo'); save_system('demo', fullfile(pwd, 'demo.slx'));
tools.notes: Use visdiff or the Comparison Tool for diffs, since the content is compressed. Models saved in newer releases can be exported for older ones with Simulink.exportToVersion.

tools.name: .mdl
tools.description: Legacy Simulink model file: a single plain-text file of nested parameter blocks. Still readable and writable, useful for text diffs, but new features may require SLX.
tools.usage: save_system(mdl, 'model.mdl')
tools.example: save_system('demo', 'demo.mdl');   % convert SLX to MDL
tools.notes: A model cannot exist as both .slx and .mdl with the same name on the path without shadowing warnings.

tools.name: .slxp
tools.description: Protected model created with Simulink.ModelReference.protect: an obfuscated package that can be simulated, viewed and/or used for code generation through a Model block without exposing its contents.
tools.usage: Simulink.ModelReference.protect(model, 'Mode', 'CodeGeneration')
tools.example:
Simulink.ModelReference.protect('ctrl', 'Mode', 'Normal');
% ctrl.slxp can now be referenced: set_param('top/Ctrl', 'ModelName', 'ctrl.slxp')
tools.notes: Can be password protected per capability (view, simulate, generate code).

tools.name: .slxc
tools.description: Simulink cache file created next to a model when it is built or simulated as a referenced model or in accelerator modes. It stores compiled simulation and code-generation artifacts so later builds and team members can skip rebuilds.
tools.usage: Generated automatically in the cache folder (Simulink.fileGenControl / CacheFolder preference)
tools.example: Simulink.fileGenControl('set', 'CacheFolder', fullfile(tempdir, 'slcache'), 'createDir', true);
tools.notes: Safe to delete; usually excluded from source control or shared through a cache server.

tools.name: .sldd
tools.description: Simulink data dictionary: persistent storage for design data, configuration sets and enumerations shared by models, with change tracking and references between dictionaries.
tools.usage: Simulink.data.dictionary.create('data.sldd') | set_param(mdl, 'DataDictionary', 'data.sldd')
tools.example:
dd = Simulink.data.dictionary.open('project.sldd');
show(dd);   % open in Model Explorer
tools.notes: Dictionaries can be compared and merged with the Comparison Tool.

tools.name: .slreqx
tools.description: Requirements Toolbox requirement set file containing requirements, references and custom attributes. Links from other artifacts are stored in separate .slmx link set files next to the source.
tools.usage: slreq.new('reqs') | slreq.load('reqs.slreqx')
tools.example:
rs = slreq.load('CruiseReqs.slreqx');
slreq.editor;
tools.notes: Keep .slreqx and .slmx files under source control with the models they relate to.

tools.name: .mldatx
tools.description: MATLAB data container used by several Simulink tools: Simulink Test test files and results, Simulation Data Inspector sessions, Simscape logs streamed to disk and Test Manager result sets.
tools.usage: sltest.testmanager.load('tests.mldatx') | Simulink.sdi.load('session.mldatx') | simscape.logging.import('log.mldatx')
tools.example:
Simulink.sdi.save('baseline.mldatx');
sltest.testmanager.load('regression.mldatx');
tools.notes: The owning tool is determined by the content; open with the corresponding loader function.

tools.name: .cvt
tools.description: Simulink Coverage data file containing cvtest settings and cvdata results saved with cvsave, used to archive, cumulate and report coverage later.
tools.usage: cvsave('file.cvt', cvdata) | [tests, data] = cvload('file.cvt')
tools.example:
cvsave('nightly.cvt', cov);
[~, data] = cvload('nightly.cvt');
tools.notes: Loading requires the corresponding model to be available.

tools.name: .sltx
tools.description: Simulink template file capturing a model or project with preconfigured settings, blocks and data, from which new models are created. Templates appear in the Simulink Start Page.
tools.usage: Simulink.exportToTemplate(model, 'myTemplate.sltx') | Simulink.createFromTemplate('myTemplate.sltx')
tools.example:
Simulink.exportToTemplate('companyBase', 'companyBase.sltx');
h = Simulink.createFromTemplate('companyBase.sltx');
tools.notes: Put templates on the MATLAB path so they show up in the Start Page.

tools.name: .ssc
tools.description: Simscape language source file defining a component, domain or function with parameters, variables, nodes and equations. Built into block libraries with ssc_build or used directly via the Simscape Component block; ssc_protect produces protected .sscp files.
tools.usage: +pkg/myComponent.ssc -> ssc_build('pkg')
tools.example:
% +Thermal/lossyMass.ssc
% component lossyMass
%   nodes, A = foundation.thermal.thermal; end
%   ...
% end
ssc_build('Thermal');
tools.notes: Source is plain text and diff-friendly; keep it under source control rather than the generated library.

tools.name: .sfx
tools.description: Standalone Stateflow chart file that runs in MATLAB without Simulink: the chart becomes a MATLAB object whose step method executes it, useful for application logic, UI state machines and testing chart logic.
tools.usage:
edit myChart.sfx   % create/open
ch = myChart('param', value); step(ch, 'input', x)
tools.notes: Standalone charts use MATLAB action language and support absolute-time operators such as at(n, sec) and every(n, sec).
